sources.title: A Concordande to the Texts in the Indus Script

citation.title: A Concordande to the Texts in the Indus Script
citation.publisher: Department of Asian and African Studies, University of Helsinki

access.retrieval_instructions: Download the official final published PDF from the University of Helsinki portal. Require application/pdf content, a PDF signature, 201 pages, exactly 16,767,043 bytes, and the pinned SHA-256 before use. Keep rank numbers, invariant identification numbers, page coordinates, doubt marks, and printed sign forms as separate source observations.

rights.statement: The official University of Helsinki research-portal record labels the final published version CC BY. Attribution, a license link, and an indication of changes are required. The licence does not make the publication's catalog assertions ground truth.

provenance.description: Official scan of the 1982 sign list and concordance by Kimmo Koskenniemi and Asko Parpola.
provenance.quality_notes: Printed pages 20-21 contain a sign list with repeated rank numbers above distinct invariant identification numbers. These are separate source fields, not proof of linguistic identity or allography. Concordance renderings are catalog evidence rather than direct artifact images, and their layout does not establish reading direction.

sources.title: Corpus of Texts in the Indus Script

citation.title: Corpus of Texts in the Indus Script
citation.publisher: Department of Asian and African Studies, University of Helsinki

access.retrieval_instructions: Download only the official final PDF linked by the University of Helsinki record. Require application/pdf content, a PDF signature, 180 PDF pages, exactly 16,935,356 bytes, and the pinned SHA-256. PDF pages 2-180 each contain one 4880 by 7010 one-bit image; verify native page pixels against the closed page map before layout work.

rights.statement: The official University of Helsinki research-portal record labels the final published version CC BY. Attribution, a license link, and an indication of changes are required. Open licensing permits reproducible source processing but does not make catalog assertions or machine proposals ground truth.

provenance.description: Official scan of the 1979 base corpus and its sorted-from-end and sorted-from-beginning reprints by Kimmo Koskenniemi and Asko Parpola.
provenance.quality_notes: PDF pages 22-78 contain the base identifier-order corpus, 79-128 the normal sorted-from-end rendering, 129-130 auxiliary catalog grids rather than linguistic sequences, and 131-180 the sorted-from-beginning rendering. The three renderings provide a high-value internal consistency check but share authorship and catalog lineage and are not independent historical evidence.

sources.title: Documentation and Duplicates of the Texts in the Indus Script

citation.title: Documentation and Duplicates of the Texts in the Indus Script
citation.publisher: Department of Asian and African Studies, University of Helsinki

access.retrieval_instructions: Download only the official final PDF linked by the University of Helsinki record. Require application/pdf content, a PDF signature, 98 PDF pages, exactly 8,143,483 bytes, and the pinned SHA-256. Treat the embedded OCR layer as search assistance only; identifiers, punctuation, ranges, suffixes, and group boundaries require page-image verification.

rights.statement: The official University of Helsinki research-portal record labels the final published version CC BY. Attribution, a license link, and an indication of changes are required. The publication's strict and loose duplicate relations are source assertions, not automatic physical-object identities.

provenance.description: Official 1980 continuation containing corrections and additions, Finnish-Mahadevan cross-references, documentation, and strict/loose duplicate lists.
provenance.quality_notes: Data-bearing ranges are PDF pages 20-23, 27-32, 40-51, and 59-98. The OCR layer demonstrably confuses digits and section numbers. Duplicate groups can continue across columns and pages and include information-redundancy relations that must not be collapsed into same-physical-object identity.

sources.title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access Indus records

citation.title: The Met Collection API and Open Access collection

access.retrieval_instructions: Query the official object endpoint and admit only item records whose current API response has isPublicDomain=true. Preserve the exact duplicate-key-free API response, exact official policy/API documentation snapshots, retrieval time, and the received bytes and SHA-256 of every downloaded image. Reject redirects and recheck the item flag on every new snapshot.

rights.statement: The Met makes images of public-domain artworks identified as Open Access available under CC0. Admission is item-level: a record must retain isPublicDomain=true at retrieval time. This entry does not grant rights to records or images outside that flag.

provenance.description: Official museum metadata and image endpoints for individually reviewed Indus-related collection records.
provenance.quality_notes: The listed public API object records were reviewed and exposed isPublicDomain=true at review time. Provider image order does not establish a physical side or seal/impression relation. Museum dating and cultural attribution are source assertions; secure findspot and excavation context are absent. Recheck every item flag and exact rights evidence before any release.

sources.title: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access Indus records

citation.title: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API

access.retrieval_instructions: Query the official artwork endpoint and admit only records whose current share_license_status is exactly CC0. Preserve the exact duplicate-key-free API response, exact official policy/API documentation snapshots, and every enumerated print/full derivative as a separate provider view with received byte count and SHA-256. Reject redirects and recheck the item flag on every new snapshot.

rights.statement: The reviewed official API records explicitly return share_license_status=CC0 and provide open-access image derivatives. Admission is restricted to item responses retaining that status; other museum content is not covered by this entry.

provenance.description: Official museum metadata, full-resolution TIFFs, and alternate views for individually reviewed Indus seals.
provenance.quality_notes: The listed public API accession records were reviewed and exposed share_license_status=CC0 at review time. Provider-declared byte counts are metadata rather than integrity evidence, and alternate views have no physical-side label. Secure archaeological findspot and stratigraphy are absent. Recheck every item status and exact rights evidence before any release.

citation.title: Corpus of Indus Seals and Inscriptions digitization

access.retrieval_instructions: Clone the repository outside this project, check out revision ad2f1e218a34b8c33c57de0d6cb8d99272765bbb, and run the mayig importer against its corpus directory. Do not vendor upstream files.

rights.statement: The repository declares MIT for its contents. This benchmark imports only structured transcription metadata and no images. CISI-derived record provenance and third-party catalog or image rights still require review.

provenance.description: Work-in-progress JSON digitization derived from CISI numbering and catalog observations, using upstream P identifiers and feature vectors.
provenance.quality_notes: Reviewed revision has 179 Mohenjo-daro unicorn-seal records, 1,003 token observations, no images, and no material, period, stratigraphic, findspot, or duplicate-family metadata. Two damage feature values exceed the documented 0-100 range.
